statement.excerpt: Nobody Can Measure AI’s Return On Investment Because It Doesn’t Have One

our_interpretation: In context, AI means deployed generative AI, and ROI means a positive financial return to an adopting organization.
The ordinary reading is that no organization has demonstrated benefits exceeding its AI investment and operating costs as of June 2, 2026.
A counterexample must account for implementation, integration, training, operation, and human review. Revenue gains or estimated time savings alone do not establish net ROI.
This is a general claim about AI adoption, not a claim about a named company's financial metric; metric_scope is therefore null.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes that relevant deployments have no positive net return and that this absence explains the alleged inability to measure ROI. A collection of unsuccessful projects alone cannot establish the universal claim.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one credible deployment record establishes a measured positive financial return, after full implementation and operating costs, for activity occurring by the post date.
